title: Nvidia and Samsung Join Mecka AI's $60M Robotics Data Round
summary:
The firm's annualized sales topped $100M in June and are projected to reach $300M by December. Mecka earns this revenue by employing individuals to wear body sensors while performing tasks such as repairing cars or making coffee to create training sets for humanoid robots. New strategic backers joining the venture include Nvidia, Samsung, Microsoft's M12 venture fund, and Qualcomm Ventures, as well as operators Tony Xu and Frank Slootman.

These investments are part of a $60M Series B round led by Sequoia that brings the company's total funding to over $120M. The capital will scale a computer vision lab that converts raw motion footage into structured training signals and supports the production of custom multi-sensor capture hardware. The startup aims to build the first internet-scale dataset for physical AI to serve as a deployment layer for general purpose robotics.

We @sequoia are thrilled to lead @MeckaAI’s Series B. AI took the digital world by storm; bringing it into the physical world will be a wave at least as large, but harder - it demands excellence across research, hardware, software, operations and deployment.

That is the mission @joshavata, @jasontheutopian and the Mecka AI team have taken on: helping physical AI labs, robotics companies and enterprises reach physical AGI, as their partner for training data, RL and deployment. They built differentiated advantages in each discipline and combined them into a strong, scalable and flexible platform that has helped them win over many of the leading AI labs and robotics companies and quickly become the emerging leader in this category.

That is why we are excited to back them, and why NVIDIA, Samsung, Microsoft and Qualcomm joined the round, alongside exceptional founders and operators including Tony Xu, Frank Slootman, Milan Kovac, Jonathan Chadwick and many more.

selectedTweets.text:
Moravec's paradox, restated as a data problem.

We digitized human knowledge, and machines learned to reason. Nobody digitized how a hand grips, folds or pours.

Mecka's bet is that robots don't lack intelligence, they lack experience, and that experience has to be recorded from humans first. A year ago that bet was controversial but Sequoia is now leading their $60M Series B.

selectedTweets.text:
Robotics doesn't have an internet-scale dataset. That's the real bottleneck.

Mecka just raised a $60M Series B, led by Sequoia, to build one.

> custom multi-sensor capture hardware
> a computer vision lab turning raw, noisy footage into structured training signal
> hiring engineers to scale both

A single second of reality holds more information than a page of text. That's the scale of the job.
